newsitem.title: JAPAN: N.Korea denies murder of S.Korean consul in Russia.
newsitem.headline: N.Korea denies murder of S.Korean consul in Russia.

text.p: Communist North Korea on Friday denied that it was involved in the murder of a South Korean diplomat in Russia's Far East city of Vladivostok earlier this week.
"(South Korea) is framing a despicable plot to link our country (to the incident)," North Korea's official newspaper Rodong Sinmun said.
The newspaper statement, North Korea's first reaction to the killing of the South Korean diplomat, was broadcast by Radio Pyongyang, monitored by the Tokyo-based Radiopress news agency.
Seoul said on Wednesday that Choi Duck-keun, the South Korean consul in Vladivostok, was found bludgeoned to death outside his apartment on Tuesday.
South Korean media reports suggested that North Korea was behind the killing of Choi, who was responsible for North Korean affairs and security at the consulate.
South Korean diplomats have been warned to take extra precautions following a threat by North Korea to retaliate unless Seoul returned a submarine that intruded into the South's waters two weeks ago.

Pyongyang has demanded the immediate return of the vessel along with its surviving and dead crew. An estimated 26 North Koreans were in the the submarine, and of that, 22 have been killed and one captured alive during a manhunt.
